merger_description:
Imaging Associates Radiology Pty Ltd (**IA Radiology**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Country Radiology Pty Ltd trading as Sunraysia Radiology (**Sunraysia Radiology**).

IA Radiology is a wholly owned subsidiary of Radia Group Pty Ltd (**Imaging Associates**), which is majority owned by a combination of funds managed by private equity firm Advent Partners Pty Ltd (**Advent Partners**), together with other shareholders comprising radiologists and management of Imaging Associates.

Imaging Associates provides on-site diagnostic imaging (**DI**) services from 28 private clinics (including private hospitals) in metropolitan and regional Melbourne, metropolitan Adelaide and Wagga Wagga in the Riverina region of New South Wales. Imaging Associates also provides DI services to public hospitals, and teleradiology services.

Sunraysia Radiology is an independent provider of on-site DI services operating from a single private clinic in Mildura, Victoria. Sunraysia Radiology does not provide any services to public hospitals or private hospitals and does not provide teleradiology services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between IA Radiology and
Sunraysia Radiology in the supply of DI services in the
Mildura region
b. there are alternative suppliers of DI services in Mildura and
the surrounding region.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
